purpose: Sound-design intelligence for premium motion. Audio supports rhythm and continuity but never overrides readability, factual truth or voice clarity.

beatGrid.rule: Use beat/bar sync when music-led, but visual meaning and factual reading time beat forced synchronization.

productionRules: Use licensed, first-party or otherwise authorized audio only.
Do not infer usage rights from public availability.
Do not fabricate location-specific ambience and present it as real documentary sound.
Do not imply an official vehicle through engine/vehicle sound if no verified official vehicle is present.
Voice/testimony remains primary; duck music and SFX around speech.
Do not sonify every action. Silence and holds are legitimate premium choices.
Avoid generic corporate music by default; choose musical character from the brief and active brand context.
Avoid the same whoosh/pop on every transition or node.
Alert sound must remain calm/civic unless the factual situation truly warrants emergency treatment.
Music/SFX are never required to make a piece production-ready; missing recommended audio is a warning, not permission to use rights-unknown assets.
selectionProtocol: 2. Read only its matching sound-design preset.
3. If a licensed/approved music bed exists, build a BPM frame grid before final timing.
4. Select only cue roles that support specific storyboard beats.
5. Keep hero cue count low; do not impact every title/metric.
6. Verify audio license/provenance before production use.
7. Check voice/music balance, critical-copy reading time and transition sync during final visual+audio review.
